authority: AGENTS.md, 'The core owns the map, not the blades', ruled by the human on 2026-10-04. Ground cover is recorded as a plant type and a density and is interpreted per client. A planting is core-owned as an individual only when it stands at a place that has a name, and that is derived from its position rather than declared on it; see the `planting` block.

density.client_may: grow denser grass, draw blades a player can walk through, wind a wave across the meadow, batch into patches or scatter per cell, or not draw ground cover at all. None of that is the core's to say.

reference_kit.status: a reference, not authority. Appearance is the client's under the 2026-10-04 ruling, so the two *_per_m2 figures are ONE interpretation derived from this kit's measured crown and a client may replace both the kit and the numbers. cover_fraction does not depend on it.

rule.closure: A closed meadow has no bare ground between the crowns of its plants, so the lattice pitch is the crown diameter. Crowns of diameter d on a square lattice cover pi (d/2)^2 / d^2 = pi/4 of the ground, whatever d is, so cover_fraction is a property of the rule and not of any asset.
rule.coverage: Flowers are not a closure. The references' ground is a median 11.1% saturated non-green, measured by shared/geometry/meadow_census.py and recorded in MEADOW-ASSESSMENT.md section 1, and a clump of diameter d covers pi (d/2)^2 of it.
rule.not_a_parameter: There is no 'how much grass' number anywhere in the core. Both figures fall out of a rule and a measured diameter, and changing the diameter changes them.
rule.plants_per_m2: cover_fraction / (pi (d/2)^2), which for the closure is 1 / d^2

forest_slope.why: forest-slope ground above the map treeline or steeper than the map vegetation slope limit: exposed high country and rock faces, rather than all forest soil.

tracks.why: the cells a track polyline runs through, tested against half the cell's own diagonal so the test needs no width the map does not publish. THE TRACK WIDTH IS A KNOWN GAP: worldmap.json tracks carry id, serves and polyline and nothing else, so this carves the line and not the worn margin beside it.

village_footprint.why: the one deliberate cluster's own footprint_radius_m. Graded ground, not meadow.

water.why: the river's and the lake's own wetted cells, at the plan's water distance of zero. The bank beyond the water IS stamped: it is meadow, and grass at a river's edge is what a river's edge looks like.

grid.row_order: row 0 is MINIMUM y: y = offset_xy_m[1] + row * quad_size_m, matching GridSpec. The committed rasters use row 0 = MAX y; this file does not, and the difference is stated rather than left to be guessed.

mask.encoding: run-lengths over the grid in row-major order, alternating uncovered then covered, so runs[0] is a run of zeros and the covered runs are the odd numbered ones. The sum of runs is resolution * resolution.

not_stamped_note: Each excluded cell is counted under its first failed test, so the four exclusion counts sum to the unstamped area. `zones` is measured by the same tree_zone_at this file uses; its stamped counts and `mask.stamped_cells` must agree and shared/tests/test_ground_cover.py says so.

named_place.a_gate_needs_no_field: The ruling names a gate, and there is no gate in the world today. None is needed, because a gate is a placed structure and a placed structure stands either on a homestead's screen or inside the village footprint — both already in the table above. A gate added to placement.json is covered by the derivation the moment it is added.
named_place.extents: No new numbers. A homestead is within tree_rule.homestead_screen_m (45 m) of a homestead centre; a village is within village.footprint_radius_m (77.5 m) of the village centre; a river or a lake is a cell the plan already measures at water_distance <= 0, which is the water plus each body's published bank_m (30 m). Each is a figure worldmap.json already publishes and already uses to answer a different question about the same ground, so there is no second set of radii to drift.
named_place.test: A planting is core-owned when it stands at a place that has a name — a homestead, a village, a gate, a river — because then the place is what you find and the plant only marks it. If the place is findable without the plant, the plant is the client's to draw. DECORATIVE IS NOT THE TEST; FINDABLE IS.
named_place.why_no_field: The test is derivable from the instance's own position and the published map, so it is derived rather than declared. A declared tag can be forgotten, and a forgotten tag silently makes a findable plant stamped — a quiet wrong answer. A derived test cannot be forgotten, because there is nothing to remember. This answers the question the human raised against the earlier `landmark` tag.
named_place.worked_case: A wildflower clump in open meadow is stamped, because the meadow is findable without it. The same species planted beside a homestead is core-owned, because the homestead is a name. So the stamp does not make an individual flower inexpressible: it records that flowers are the stamped case by default and says exactly how a findable one is recognised instead.

pin.asserts: that the asset is core-owned as an individual. A pin records a decision the core cannot derive; it is not a second opinion on one it can.
pin.for: the cases named_place cannot reach: the asset is not a planting at all — a bollard, a cairn, a beached hull, a surveyor's stake — or the place has no name yet, such as a well to be sunk or a boundary not yet run.
pin.not_reachable_here: The waymarker case — a planting put down to mark something not yet there — is HELD by the human and is deliberately not implemented. A pin is not that field under another name: a pin asserts about a place, and marks_future says the place does not exist yet, which is a different claim from marking one that does. Nothing in this file can express a waymarker.
pin.refused_where: ONLY where the core has no name for the place. Where the place already has a name the dividing line has already decided, a pin there is redundant, and an instance carrying one is REFUSED. That is the junk-drawer guard, and it is the one that must not be violable silently.
pin.supersedes: the earlier per-kind `landmark` tag, which stood where this test is derivable. There is one mechanism and it is general.

planting.why: AGENTS.md, 'The core owns the map, not the blades': the core records the plant type and the density for ground cover and plant life is not persisted per item. These are the assets the removed per-item scheme placed, named so that putting one back is detectable rather than merely discouraged.
